subject: Two of Eden's rivers still flow today
preview: The other two are an honest mystery. Here is what Genesis says.
linkText: The Garden of Eden & the Four Rivers Explained

blocks.text: You have probably seen the graphic.
A garden. One river flowing out of it.
Then that river splitting into four.
Maybe it even had a little map, pinning exactly where Eden sat.
But here is the catch.
A lot of what gets shared online adds details Genesis never gives.
And it skips right past the details Genesis actually does give.
So I want to take you back to Genesis 2.
Here are the four rivers, exactly as the text names them.
🟢 Pison: flows around Havilah, a land of gold, bdellium and onyx stone.
🟢 Gihon: flows around the land the King James Bible calls Ethiopia.
🟢 Hiddekel: flows east of Assyria, widely agreed to be the Tigris.
🟢 Euphrates: named plainly, because the first readers already knew it.
Two of them you can find on a map right now. The Tigris and the Euphrates still run through the Middle East.
The other two are an honest mystery. No river today has been proven to be the Pison or the Gihon.
But most graphics stop right there.
They never show you what happened next.
After Adam and Eve sinned, God placed Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
The tree was not gone. The way to it was guarded.
Then, in the very last chapter of the Bible, that same tree of life shows up again. This time the gates stand open.
What sin closed in a garden, Christ reopens in a city.
The Bible ends right where it began.
In the full guide I walk through Eden, the two trees, all four rivers by name, and how Genesis 2 connects to Revelation 22. And I am honest about where the text stops and the guesswork begins.
